name: Gelatin
description: Gelling agent made from collagen in animal skin, bones and connective tissue.
possible_origin: Pork, beef, fish or poultry. The E-number alone does not say which.
halal_assessment: Depends entirely on the animal source and, for land animals, on how the animal was slaughtered.
reason: Gelatin is always animal-derived, but the label does not state which animal it comes from.
verification_advice: Look for the declared source (fish, halal beef) or a halal certificate, or ask the manufacturer.
source: E-number identity: EU food additive list. Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Pork gelatin
description: Gelatin made from pig skin or bones.
halal_assessment: Animal-derived; pork origin is prohibited.
reason: The label explicitly declares pork as the source of the gelatin, and pork is prohibited.
verification_advice: Avoid, or choose a product made with fish, halal beef or plant-based gelling agents such as agar or pectin.
source: Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Pork and pork derivatives
description: Meat, fat and other products from pigs.
halal_assessment: Pork and its derivatives are prohibited.
reason: The ingredient is explicitly identified as coming from pork.
verification_advice: Avoid this product.
source: Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Alcoholic beverage
description: An intoxicating drink used as an ingredient.
possible_origin: Fermented or distilled grapes, grains or sugar.
halal_assessment: Intoxicating beverages are prohibited as ingredients under mainstream halal standards.
reason: The ingredient is explicitly identified as an alcoholic beverage.
verification_advice: Avoid, unless the label shows it is only a non-alcoholic flavouring; in that case verify with the manufacturer.
source: Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Ethanol (alcohol)
description: Used as a solvent or carrier for flavourings and extracts, and present naturally in small amounts after fermentation.
possible_origin: Synthetic, or fermented from grain, sugar or fruit.
halal_assessment: Requires context: its source, its purpose and the amount left in the final product all matter, and certification bodies set different limits.
reason: Alcohol is listed, but the label does not show its type, purpose or remaining amount.
verification_advice: Check whether it is a processing aid or an added ingredient, and follow the limits of the certification body you trust.
source: Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Lecithin
description: Emulsifier that helps oil and water mix; common in chocolate and baked goods.
possible_origin: Usually soy or sunflower; can also come from egg yolk or animal fat.
halal_assessment: Plant and egg lecithin raise no concern; lecithin from animal fat depends on the animal and its slaughter.
reason: Lecithin may be plant or animal derived, and the label does not state the source.
verification_advice: Look for 'soy lecithin' or 'sunflower lecithin' on the label, or ask the manufacturer.
source: E-number identity: EU food additive list. Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Glycerin (glycerol)
description: Humectant and sweetener that keeps food moist.
possible_origin: Vegetable oils, animal fats or synthetic production.
halal_assessment: Vegetable and synthetic glycerin raise no concern; glycerin from animal fat depends on the animal and its slaughter.
reason: Glycerin can have different origins, and the label does not state which.
verification_advice: Look for 'vegetable glycerin' on the label, or ask the manufacturer for the source.
source: E-number identity: EU food additive list. Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids

mono and diglycerides of fatty acids
description: Emulsifier used in bread, margarine, ice cream and biscuits.
possible_origin: Vegetable oils (palm, soy, rapeseed) or animal fats (beef or pork).
halal_assessment: Plant-derived E471 raises no concern; animal-derived E471 depends on the animal and its slaughter.
reason: E471 can be plant or animal derived, and the code alone does not reveal the source.

name: Stearic acid and stearates
description: Fatty acids and their salts, used as anti-caking agents and in chewing gum and sweets.
halal_assessment: Plant-derived stearates raise no concern; animal-derived ones depend on the animal and its slaughter.
reason: Stearates can be plant or animal derived, and the label does not state the source.
verification_advice: Look for a declared vegetable origin or ask the manufacturer.
source: E-number identity: EU food additive list. Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Carmine (cochineal)
description: Red colouring used in sweets, yoghurts and drinks.
halal_assessment: Insect-derived colouring; scholars and certification bodies differ on whether it is permissible.
reason: Carmine is made from insects, and opinions on insect-derived colourings differ.
verification_advice: Follow the position of the scholar or certification body you trust, or choose a product with a plant-based colour.
source: E-number identity: EU food additive list. Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Shellac
description: Glazing agent that gives sweets and fruit a shiny coating.
possible_origin: Resin secreted by the lac insect; often dissolved in alcohol during processing.
halal_assessment: Insect-derived; scholars and certification bodies differ, and the processing solvent may also matter.
reason: Shellac comes from an insect secretion, and opinions on it differ.
verification_advice: Follow the position of the scholar or certification body you trust.
source: E-number identity: EU food additive list. Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: L-cysteine
description: Flour treatment agent used to soften dough.
possible_origin: Human hair, poultry feathers, pig bristles, or fermentation and synthetic production.
halal_assessment: Depends on the source; fermentation-derived and synthetic L-cysteine raise no concern.
reason: L-cysteine has several possible sources, some of which are not permissible, and the label does not state which.
verification_advice: Ask the manufacturer whether it is synthetic or made by fermentation.
source: E-number identity: EU food additive list. Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Edible bone phosphate
description: Anti-caking agent and mineral supplement.
halal_assessment: Depends on the animal and, for cattle, on its slaughter.
reason: Bone phosphate is animal-derived, and the label does not state which animal.
verification_advice: Ask the manufacturer for the animal source or look for a halal certificate.
source: E-number identity: EU food additive list. Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Disodium inosinate
description: Flavour enhancer used in snacks, instant noodles and seasonings.
possible_origin: Meat or fish extracts, or fermentation of plant sugars.
halal_assessment: Fermentation-derived E631 raises no concern; meat-derived E631 depends on the animal and its slaughter.
reason: E631 can be made from meat, fish or by fermentation, and the label does not state which.
verification_advice: Ask the manufacturer how it is produced or look for a vegetarian mark.
source: E-number identity: EU food additive list. Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Rennet
description: Enzymes used to curdle milk when making cheese.
possible_origin: Calf stomach, or microbial and plant sources.
halal_assessment: Microbial and plant rennet raise no concern; on animal rennet scholars differ depending on the slaughter.
reason: Rennet may be animal or microbial, and the label does not state which.
verification_advice: Look for 'microbial rennet' or 'vegetarian rennet' on the label, or a halal certificate.
source: Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Cheese and whey
description: Dairy products made by curdling milk; whey is the liquid left over.
possible_origin: Milk, curdled with animal, microbial or plant rennet.
halal_assessment: The milk itself raises no concern; the question is the rennet used to curdle it.
reason: Cheese and whey are made with rennet, whose source is not stated on the label.
verification_advice: Look for 'microbial rennet', a vegetarian mark or a halal certificate.
source: Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Meat and animal fat
description: Meat, fat or extracts from permissible land animals and poultry.
halal_assessment: The animal is permissible, but the meat is halal only if it was slaughtered according to Islamic requirements.
reason: The product contains meat or animal fat, and the ingredient list cannot show how the animal was slaughtered.
verification_advice: Look for a halal certificate that covers the meat.
source: Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Flavourings (unspecified)
description: Substances added for taste or smell; the label does not have to list what they contain.
possible_origin: Plant extracts, synthetic compounds, or occasionally animal-derived substances; often carried in alcohol.
halal_assessment: Most flavourings raise no concern, but the composition and the carrier solvent are not disclosed.

verification_advice: Ask the manufacturer whether the flavouring contains animal-derived substances or alcohol.
source: Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.

name: Vinegar

source: Halal assessment: general guidance; consult a recognised halal certification body.
